nodes.summary: Let $P \ge 1$ be an integer and let $U_n = U_n(P, -1)$ be the Lucas sequence with $U_0 = 0$, $U_1 = 1$ and $U_{n+2} = PU_{n+1} + U_n$. Then there is an integer $K > 0$ such that for every natural number $n$ the three integers $U_n + K - 1$, $U_n + K$ and $U_n + K + 1$ are all composite, that is, each is greater than $1$ and not prime.
nodes.title: A shift of $U_n(P, -1)$ away from primes

nodes.summary: Let $F_n$ be the $n$-th Fibonacci number, with $F_0 = 0$, $F_1 = 1$ and $F_{n+2} = F_{n+1} + F_n$. For every natural number $n$, the number $F_n + 14475$ is not prime.
nodes.title: Fibonacci numbers shifted by $14475$ are never prime

nodes.summary: Let $x \ne y$ be real numbers such that $x + y$ and $xy$ are integers, and let $r > 1$ be a natural number. Let $P$ and $Q$ be integers with $P = x^r + y^r$ and $Q = x^r y^r$, and suppose $Q \ne 0$, $P \ge 1$ and $P^2 - 4Q > 0$. Let $U_n = U_n(P, Q)$ be the Lucas sequence with $U_0 = 0$, $U_1 = 1$ and $U_{n+2} = PU_{n+1} - QU_n$. Then $|U_n|$ is prime for only finitely many natural numbers $n$.
nodes.title: Lucas sequences with power parameters have finitely many prime terms

nodes.summary: Let $P \ge 3$ be an integer and let $U_n = U_n(P, 1)$ be the Lucas sequence with $U_0 = 0$, $U_1 = 1$ and $U_{n+2} = PU_{n+1} - U_n$. Then there is a natural number $N$ such that for every $n \ge N$ the three integers $U_n - 1$, $U_n$ and $U_n + 1$ are all composite, that is, each is greater than $1$ and not prime.
nodes.title: Unit shifts of $U_n(P, 1)$ are eventually composite

nodes.summary: Let $P$ and $Q$ be integers with $P \ge 1$ and $P^2 - 4Q > 0$, where $Q \ne 0$ is a perfect square, and let $U_n = U_n(P, Q)$ be the Lucas sequence with $U_0 = 0$, $U_1 = 1$ and $U_{n+2} = PU_{n+1} - QU_n$. Then $|U_n|$ is prime for only finitely many natural numbers $n$.
nodes.title: Lucas sequences with square $Q$ have finitely many prime terms

nodes.summary: Let $U_n = U_n(3, -4)$ be the Lucas sequence with $U_0 = 0$, $U_1 = 1$ and $U_{n+2} = 3U_{n+1} + 4U_n$, so that $U_n = 0, 1, 3, 13, 51, 205, 819, \ldots$. For every natural number $n \ge 4$, $U_n$ is composite: $U_n > 1$ and $U_n$ is not prime.
nodes.title: Composite terms of the Lucas sequence $U_n(3, -4)$
